name: Berks County, Pennsylvania (United States)
description: Vertical tricolour of red, white and blue overlaid by a large yellow lozenge bearing a black-line drawing of a plough, wheat sheaf and grass, with the date 1752 in the upper hoist and the name Berks in the lower fly.
history: Berks County (Pennsylvania German: Barricks Kaundi) is a county in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. The flag was adopted in 1941 (designed in 1914 by Charles K. Snell of Reading and officially adopted in 1941 by the County Commissioners, according to Flags of the World quoting the county website).

features.role: lozenge shaped like the county, with a plough and wheat sheaf
